title: Extensibility Options for Third-Party Payments
author: AnetaChuda
text:
Introduction 
 Please note that the feature of this blog post is only for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. 
 When importing third-party payment files or return files via the Manage Incoming Payment Files app (F1680) the system parses the file and maps the raw data to internal structures using the Map Format data app. However, the default mapping may not always fit your specific business requirements. 
 Two Business Add-In (BAdI) extension points are delivered to adjust the mapped data at batch header and item level. Before the mapped data is written to the staging tables — you can change these values according to the business requirements. 
 The adjusted staging data is then consumed in the second step by the Process Imported Third-Party Payments app, which creates the actual Contract Accounting payment lots and return lots. Any changes you have made in the BAdI are therefore reflected in the final posted lot. This blog post introduces the procedure of importing and processing the external files. You can also learn about how to adjust the mapped data using the BadIs. For more information about the related blog posts, see the following links: 
 Payment Lot Data Import via Third-Party Payments - SAP Community 
 Return Lot File Import via Third- Party Payments - SAP Community 
 Where the Extension Point Runs 
 The diagram below shows the flow after you get the external files to the posting lots in Contract Accounting: 

 The external file is first uploaded via the Manage Incoming Payment Files app, where the Map Format Data for Third Party Payments app transform the bank/collector-specific (external) format into internal structures. 
 After this mapping, the corresponding Badi is triggered, when you can adjust the data, before the data is written to the staging tables. 
 Then you use the Process Imported Third-Party Payments app to pick up the staging data and create the final Payment Lot or Return Lot. 
 Business Add-Ins 
 BAdI for Payment Lot Import — BADI_FKKID_EXPC_PAYMENT_LOT 

 This BAdI is called during the import of third-party payment files in Contract Accounting. It allows you to modify the mapped payment data before it is stored in the staging area; the adjusted data is subsequently used to create a Payment (Order) Lot in Contract Accounting. 
 BAdI for Return Lot Import — BADI_FKKID_EXPC_RETURN_LOT 

 This BAdI is called during the import of third-party return files in Contract Accounting. It allows you to modify the mapped return data before it is stored in the staging area; the adjusted data is subsequently used to create a Return Lot in Contract Accounting. 
 Note: 
 The BAdI is called once per imported batch. It receives the complete lot header and the full table of items for that batch as changing parameters. This means you can modify any field on any existing item , but you cannot add or remove items and item numbers cannot be changed . 
 Implementation: Custom Logic App 
 As a key user, you can use the cloud business add-in (BAdI) to implement your own logic. Before using the cloud BAdI, ensure that you have assigned the business role SAP_BR_EXTENSIBILITY_SPEC. 
 Note: Regarding of extensibility options for developers, go to Business Accelerator Hub and search for Adjust Payment Data (for Customer). 
 Open Custom Logic app. Select “ Create ”. 
 In the search box, search for the BAdI name: 
 For Payment Lot : BADI_FKKID_EXPC_PAYMENT_LOT 
 For Return Lot : BADI_FKKID_EXPC_RETURN_LOT and search. 
 The extension point appears in the list with its description. Select it using the radio button, then click Step 2. 
 Click Add to add a filter row. Select “Add” in the pop-up window to apply filter condition. 
 Set the connector THIRDPARTYPAYMENTFORMATTYPE equal to your format type value: 
 For Payment Lot : THIRDPARTYPAYMENTFORMATTYPE = FICA-PAYMENT-LOT 
 For Return Lot : THIRDPARTYPAYMENTFORMATTYPE = FICA-RETURN-LOT. Save the entries. 
 After you save the condition, the filter with the format is visible. This ensures the BAdI is only triggered for files of the matching format type. Click Step3. 
 Provide a meaningful description and a unique implementation ID (Create an implementation ID starting with YY1_): 
 Click Review and Create. 
 Select Publish. You can then Open Code Editor. 
 You can select Show Sample Code and copy them to clipboard to better change the coding based on your business needs. 
 Click Edit and write your implement the logic based on your business requirements, then select Save and Publish . 
 The implementation takes effect immediately on the next file import. It is not required to restart the system or transport. 
 Monitoring the Changes with Cloud BadIs 

 Upload the files after the Cloud BAdI Implementation 
 Open the Manage Incoming Payment Files (F1680) app. 
 Select Import and choose Third-party Payment to upload the files 
 Select Payment Lot Data (Contract Accounting) as format. 
 Upload the file and process. 

 View the changes in the Monitor Third-Party Payment app 
 Open the Monitor Third-Party Payment app. 
 Select row with imported file and here are results that are marked in yellow. 
 Is this blog post useful to you? Leave your comments below to let us know your thoughts.

title: Sales Order Stock (E) in SAP Logistics Management
author: marco_schaaf
text:
Introduction 
 In make-to-order (MTO) and purchase-to-order (PTO) scenarios, goods are procured or produced exclusively for a specific customer and must only be supplied to that customer. Sales Order Stock, identified by special stock type “Sales Order Stock (E)”, ensures exactly this: a quantity of a product is reserved for one sales order and item, never available for any other sales order. 
 We are pleased to announce that SAP Logistics Management now supports special stock type Sales Order Stock (E).

title: Simplified setup of Custom Document Grounding for SAP Joule for Consultants using CIAS Automation
author: vasu_jindal
text:
This blog is co-authored by colleagues from SAP AI Factory @Samir_Rai , @Ananny_Tripathi . We have received considerable support from @HartmutStraub from AI RIG, @AnaghaDAnanth , @karthikeyan Mohanachandran and @ Rahul Jain from SAP CLE and @YihsuanLin from SAP J4C product management team. 
 1. Introduction 
 SAP Joule for Consultants is a generative AI copilot built specifically for the SAP consulting community. Grounded in over 9 terabytes of curated SAP knowledge — including 18+ million pages of SAP documentation, 100+ SAP certifications, and implementation guides — it delivers expert-level answers based on trusted SAP content. 
 But every consulting organization carries its own body of knowledge: internal delivery frameworks, proprietary accelerators, client-specific runbooks, architecture decisions, and hard-won lessons that simply don't exist in SAP's public content. Custom knowledge grounding is what bridges that gap — allowing you to connect Joule to your organization's curated content so it can answer not just as an SAP expert, but as your team's expert. 
 What Custom Knowledge Grounding Does 
 Custom Knowledge Grounding extends SAP Joule for Consultants with your organization’s own documents. The documents are uploaded to a data repository, indexed by SAP AI Core Document Grounding, and retrieved at runtime to ground SAP Joule for Consultants’ answers. Users get responses that combine the SAP-curated content SAP Joule for Consultants ships with and their firm’s own methodologies, policies, and delivery standards. 

 Configuring custom knowledge grounding manually, however, involves its own set of connected steps — setting up the right services, connecting knowledge sources, configuring trust and authorization, and ensuring everything is wired together correctly in the right sequence. Done manually, this takes considerable time and leaves room for misses and misconfiguration. 
 Cloud Integration Automation Service (CIAS) changes that. In this blog, we walk through how to use CIAS to automate the setup of custom knowledge grounding for SAP Joule for Consultants — end to end, in the correct order, with a guided workflow that replaces the manual overhead with a reliable, repeatable process. 
 2. The Role of CIAS Automation 
 Cloud Integration Automation service provides you a guided workflow to activate SAP cloud solutions. The guided workflow contains instructions for manual and automated tasks to enable an easy and quick integration configuration setup. The service is also used to integrate SAP Cloud solutions to on-premises solutions or other cloud solutions. It’s a free service available for the customers. 
 For SAP Joule for Consultants, CIAS plays a key role in simplifying activation. Instead of working across multiple tools separately — SAP BTP Cockpit, SAP Cloud Identity, SAP Central Business Configuration, and SAP for Me — and having to get the sequence right yourself, CIAS provides one guided workflow that handles these tasks end-to-end, in the correct order. 
 Here’s the advantage it brings compared to the manual activation: 

 3. Subscribing SAP Cloud Integration and Automation Service (CIAS) 
 If you already have CIAS activated in any of the existing BTP subaccount, you may skip this step. The service is available in the following regions. 

 Service Platform 
 Region 

 Amazon Web Service (AWS) 
 Europe (Frankfurt) EU10 
 Europe (Frankfurt) EU Access EU11 
 US East (VA) US10 
 Australia (Sydney) AP10 
 Japan (Tokyo) JP10 
 Canada (Montreal) CA10 

 Microsoft Azure 
 Europe (Netherlands) EU20 
 China (North 3) CN20 

 Alibaba Cloud 
 China (Shanghai) CN40 

 Amazon Web Service (AWS) 
 Europe (Frankfurt) EU10 
 Europe (Frankfurt) EU Access EU11 
 US East (VA) US10 
 Australia (Sydney) AP10 
 Japan (Tokyo) JP10 
 Canada (Montreal) CA10 

 Microsoft Azure 
 Europe (Netherlands) EU20 
 China (North 3) CN20 

 Alibaba Cloud China (Shanghai) CN40 

 To subscribe to a standard plan, following are the required steps: 
 Login into your global account in the cockpit. 
 Create a subaccount in the Cloud Integration Automation service supported regions. 

 In the filters area, select the All-Types filter, and from the dropdown menu, select Cloud Integration Automation Service . 

 In the left-side menu, choose Services → Service Marketplace . All the resources you are entitled to consume in the subaccount appears as tiles. 

 Choose the Cloud Integration Automation Service tile to see the Overview page. Here, you can find more information about the application including all the available plans. 
 Choose Create . 
 In the displayed window, select the Standard plan of type subscription and choose Create . A confirmation pop-up appears with the link to the Instances and Subscriptions page , where you can follow the status of your new subscription under the Subscriptions table. 

 Once the application is subscribed, assign yourself the CIASIntegrationAdmin role so you can run the CIAS workflow. In your subaccount, go to Security > Users and select your user (default IDP or platform user). — click Role Collections on the right, then use the (...) menu and select Assign Role Collection to add the CIASIntegrationAdmin role. 

 The Go to Application link becomes available once the subscription is activated. Choose the link to launch the Cloud Integration Automation service and obtain its URL. 

 4. Prerequisites for Custom Knowledge Grounding Activation 
 SAP Joule for Consultants — an existing instance. See Onboarding Guide for SAP Joule for Consultants | SAP Help Portal . 
 SAP AI Core with the extended plan — required by Document Grounding. See SAP AI Core — SAP Discovery Center . 
 Object Store (recommended for the initial setup) — the simplest data repository to start with, and the example used throughout this mission. See Object Store — SAP Discovery Center . 
 5. Use CIAS to Set Up Joule for Consultants 
 5.1 Launch CIAS and Plan Integration Scenario 
 In the subaccount, go to Instances and Subscriptions and open the Cloud Integration Automation tool using the default identity provider. 
 This launches the CIAS instance. Select Plan Integration Scenarios . 

 In Plan Integration Scenarios , search for " SAP Joule for Consultants Document Grounding Setup " and click the arrow on the right of the result. 

 This opens the scenario details. Click Start to begin the guided workflow. 

 5.2 Select the Scope 
 Select the type of data source you want to use for grounding Joule for Consultants with your organization's custom documents. Additionally, choose whether you want to reuse an existing AI Core instance by selecting Yes , or select No if you want the automation to create a new AI Core instance for you. 

 After that click on next step. 
 5.3 Select the Systems 

 Select the SAP BTP AI core instance that you want to use for creating the pipeline for document grounding. Also select the SAP Joule for consultants application for which you are setting up Custom Knowledge grounding. 

 5.4 Add the Task Parameter 
 Now add the following task parameters: 
 Create BTP Space: Add admin credential for the BTP Global account where SAP Joule for consultants is provisioned. 
 Get Space Name for AI Core Subaccount: Provide AI core service instance name 
 Retrieve Existing Al Core Details and Create Key: Add admin credential for the BTP Global account where SAP AI core is provisioned. 

 Create Al Core resource group: Provide the name of the Resource group you want to give (e.g. J4c-custom-knowledge) 
 Create generic secret for J4C DG SharePoint in AI Core Subaccount: Provide the SharePoint Application ID, SharePoint App Client Secret, SharePoint Tenant IO, SharePoint URL 
 Create DG pipeline for Al Core SharePoint Data Source: Provide the SharePoint Side ID and If you have specific folders to be included for SAP Joule for Consultants custom Knowledge grounding, please check the include path checkbox and provide the path for the folder. 

 5.5 Review 
 Check the disclaimer checkbox and Review all the details ones and then click finish and wait for workflow to be created. 

 5.6 Monitor Integration Setup 
 Click on Monitor Integration Setup to open the workflow. 

 Ones the automation starts, wait for the automation tasks to be completed. 

 Once all the automation tasks complete, there are 3 manual steps needs to be completed in SAP Joule for Consultants: 
 Enable custom knowledge grounding in SAP Joule for Consultants: 
 Select “Enable custom knowledge grounding” task from the workflow. 

 Select view integration task 

 Ones the task opens you will be able to see the steps mentioned for how to enable custom knowledge grounding in SAP Joule for consultants. 
 Select SAP Joule for consultants console URL 

 Select settings -> Custom Knowledge Grounding -> Toggle on the button for Enable custom Knowledge grounding. 

 Click on Complete task in CIAS automation. 

 Connect to the SAP Destination Service 
 Now we will be connecting SAP destination service with the SAP Joule for consultants. 

 Go to BTP subaccount and look for j4c-dest-inst and select 1 key. 

 Copy the JSON. 

 Go back to SAP Joule for consultant console and select Custom knowledge Grounding -> Sources & Pipelines-> and click on connect 

 Select the JSON format and paste the Destination service JSON that you copied from the SAP Joule for consultants subaccount and then click on next. 

 Select the sources and then click on Save. 

 Select the complete task from the CIAS automation tool and then click on finish to complete the automation workflow. 

 Congratulations! Custom knowledge grounding is enabled in SAP Joule for Consultants. 
 Manage Sources & Pipelines 

 Monitor document grounding sources and pipelines, review pipeline status and processing information, and manage source configuration and access control. 
 Sources & Pipelines 
 In the SAP Joule for Consultants Console the selected sources appear under Sources & Pipelines . 
 The pipeline table displays the following information: 

 Column 
 Description 

 Pipeline ID 
 Unique identifier for the pipeline. Choose the link to open detailed processing logs. 

 Indexed Documents 
 Total number of documents submitted for processing. 

 Data Source 
 Type of connected data source, for example, S3. 

 Last Sync 
 Timestamp of the most recent synchronization run. 

 Status 
 Current pipeline status: Completed , Completed With Errors , or Processing . 
 Manage Sources 
 Use the action icons in the top-right corner of the page to manage the selected source: 
 Note 
 You can restrict access to each pipeline from this view using Manage Access Control . Available options are Allow All , Deny All , or Restricted to specific SAP Cloud Identity Services groups. New pipelines default to Allow All , which allows all authenticated users. 
 For more information, see Managing Access Control for Custom Knowledge Grounding on the SAP Help Portal. 
 Understand Pipeline Status 

 For details, check the documents in Bruno or in the SAP AI Launchpad. For support, open a ticket under component CA-ML-RAGE . Troubleshooting the AI Core Document Grounding pipeline is out of scope for SAP Joule for Consultants. 
 Refresh the Pipeline View and Re-Index Data 
 The Refresh icon in the console only refreshes the view. It does not re-index the data repository. 
 To make newly uploaded documents available to SAP Joule for Consultants, re-run the AI Core Document Grounding pipeline. You can do this using either of the following methods: 
 Send the restart_pipeline request as described in AI Core Document Grounding with Bruno . 
 Choose the Synchronize icon on the pipeline page as described in AI Core Document Grounding with AI Launchpad . 
 Newly uploaded documents are not indexed until the pipeline is run again and reaches FINISHED in AI Core or Completed in the SAP Joule for Consultants Console.

title: Handling Job Approval Rejection in SAP SmartRecruiters: Re-triggering Approvals via API
author: khasija
text:
Introduction 
 Job approvals in SAP SmartRecruiters ensure that every new position goes through the right authorisation chain before it is published. But what happens when an approver rejects a job — not because of a standard field change, but because they want updates that do not automatically re-trigger the approval workflow? 
 Out of the box, SmartRecruiters will only re-trigger an approval when certain protected fields are modified. If an approver rejects a job requesting a different kind of change (for example, updating the job advertisement copy or the posting location), the recruiter has no native button to restart the process. 
 This blog walks through an integration-led approach using the SmartRecruiters Approvals API and webhook events to gracefully handle rejections and re-trigger approvals programmatically — regardless of what was changed.

title: How to enable CDS CDC extraction on S/4HANA table VBFA with RUUID (RAW16) primary key?
author: albertosimeoni
text:
Hi Community, 
 I am trying to build a custom CDS extraction view on table VBFA (Sales Document Flow) in SAP S/4HANA 2025 to replicate data via ODP / Change Data Capture (CDC) into an external analytical target ( BW/4HANA embedded in SAP S/4HANA). 
 Due to the S/4HANA table restructuring of VBFA , the physical primary key in DDIC is: 

 MANDT 

 RUUID (Data Type: RAW(16) ) 
 The legacy functional business keys ( VBELV , POSNV , VBELN , POSNN , VBTYP_N ) are now regular non-key columns. 
 Approaches Attempted & Errors 
 0. automatic change data capture annotation => Fail 
 1. Manual CDC Mapping on Business Keys When attempting to define @analytics .dataExtraction.delta.changeDataCapture.mapping using the business fields: 
 @Analytics.dataExtraction.delta.changeDataCapture.mapping: [{ 
 table: 'VBFA',
 role : #MAIN,
 tableElement: [ 'VBELV', 'VBELN', 'POSNV', 'POSNN', 'VBTYP_N' ],
 viewElement: [ 'vbelv', 'vbeln', 'posnv', 'posnn', 'vbtyp_n' ]
}] 

 Result: Activation fails immediately with: 

 Error while reading CDC annotations: mapping field does not exist [Analytics] 

 Error while reading CDC annotations: No #MAIN table specified [Analytics] (The compiler rejects them because they are not physical primary key fields in table VBFA ) . 
 2. Using RUUID as Key with Automatic CDC If I define ruuid as the sole view entity key and set delta.changeDataCapture.automatic: true : 
 define view entity ZBQR_CDS_VBFA as select from vbfa {
 key ruuid,
 vbelv,
 posnv,
 vbeln,
 posnn,
 vbtyp_n,
 ...
} 

 Result: While it can compile, RAW(16) creates severe compatibility issues during replication. The consumer/target does not accept raw binary fields as unique keys for the ADSO, and converting it via bintohex(ruuid) cannot be used as an underlying table key for CDC database triggers. 
 3. Using @analytics .dataExtraction.alternativeKey I tried specifying the functional fields via @analytics .dataExtraction.alternativeKey as documented for (ABAP 8.16) while retaining key ruuid : 
 @Analytics.dataExtraction: {
 enabled: true,
 alternativeKey: ['vbelv', 'posnv', 'vbeln', 'posnn', 'vbtyp_n'],
 delta.changeDataCapture: {
 automatic: true
 }
}
define view entity ZBQR_CDS_VBFA as select from vbfa {
 key ruuid,
 vbelv,
 posnv,
 vbeln,
 posnn,
 vbtyp_n,
 ...
} 

 Result: same error as (1). 

 Another fact: 
 For the same approaches with MATDOC table the CDS view works correctly with RODPS_REPL_TEST delta extraction using BINTOHEX conversion. 
 VBFA do not pass RODPS_REPL_TEST delta extraction in any case. 
 My Questions: 

 What is the correct syntax or recommended design pattern to extract VBFA with CDC when the underlying physical key is a surrogate RAW(16) UUID and/or with BINTOHEX() function to cast RAW as STRING in SAP S/4HANA 2025 ? 

 How should @analytics .dataExtraction.alternativeKey be correctly configured in conjunction with trigger-based CDC? 

 Is trigger-based CDS CDC supported on VBFA , or is it required to fall back to a date/timestamp-based delta (or SLT)? 
 Thank you in advance for your support!

title: Advancing SAP Lakehouse and New Data Fabric Innovations in SAP Business Data Cloud for the Autonomous Enterprise
author: Irfan Khan
text:
This week at SAP TechEd Berlin , we announced new lakehouse and business data fabric capabilities to help enterprises build AI agents act with greater autonomy and confidence. 
 SAP TechEd in 2026: The Autonomous Enterprise Becomes a Reality 

 Read the innovation news guide 

 As AI is deployed across business processes, effective decision-making now hinges on unifying fragmented data and business context. AI agents can generate results quickly, but good judgement depends on deep understanding of how an organization runs. They need access to data across the enterprise, trusted views of business entities, and an understanding of the relationships, processes, and rules that define how the business operates. 

 SAP Business Data Cloud (SAP BDC) is the trusted data foundation for SAP Business AI Platform, providing a business data fabric that connects data, semantics, processes, and policies, while preserving business context that gives data meaning. The innovations announced this week extend these capabilities making enterprise data more accessible and providing agents with the trusted business context for successful AI. 

 Extend the business data fabric with an open lakehouse foundation 

 Enterprise data is distributed across sources, including databases, warehouses, and data lakes. Making that data accessible across environments often requires duplicating copies, increasing costs and making it harder to maintain consistent business context. 

 With the completed acquisition of Dremio , SAP is enhancing the open lakehouse foundation for business users and AI agents to access, share, and work with distributed data across the landscape. 

 Discover, govern, and share data across platforms: SAP BDC now supports native Apache Iceberg and a universal catalog powered by Apache Polaris, providing an open and governed data foundation for users and Joule to consume data. Together with SAP BDC Connect, this builds on SAP’s commitment to platform interoperability with zero-copy data sharing across partners including Databricks, Snowflake, Google, AWS, and Microsoft. 

 Query distributed data with zero copies: Supported by Dremio’s high-performance SQL query engine, users can federate access across lakehouses and relational databases including SQL Server, MongoDB, Oracle, and Postgres without moving data. Through integration with Joule Work, business users can ask complex questions in natural language and get answers grounded in trusted SAP and custom data products and the business context behind them, without needing to know where the data resides or how to query it. 

 Accelerate analytics and AI autonomously: For developers, maintaining query performance requires building summary tables, updating materialized views, or creating separate BI extracts to keep analytical queries fast enough for analytics and AI. This engineering work is reduced with Dremio’s Reflection technology, which learns from how your data is being used and automatically precomputes and optimizes the results your workloads need. As workloads change, Reflections adapt with them, removing the need for manual performance tuning while delivering sub-second performance at scale for analyst queries and high-concurrency agentic workloads. 

 “With SAP Business Data Cloud, we are building an enterprise foundation that unifies, governs, and is ready for innovation, so analytics and AI can scale without compromising the quality, compliance, and trust.” 
 Ganesh Sivakumar, Global Chief Data Analytics & AI Officer, Mead Johnson Nutrition 

 Accelerate your journey to the cloud 

 We also announced an expansion of the partnership with Databricks, bringing the latest set of industry-leading data platform capabilities including Lakeflow, Agent Bricks, Unity Gateway, and Lakebase to SAP Databricks in SAP Business Data Cloud. 

 SAP Application Data Foundation makes data from SAP applications available for consumption in your SAP BDC engine of choice, including SAP Databricks. This provides a cloud-native way to access data in SAP Business AI Platform, helping to lower the total cost of ownership and reduce time to value. SAP data products can subsequently be shared across the business data fabric using SAP BDC Connect for zero-copy access, avoiding the creation of additional pipelines, data copies, and silos. 

 For example, a manufacturer could use historical sales, inventory, and supply chain data to develop AI models for demand forecasting. The data is accessible from SAP BDC, where data professionals can enrich it with third-party data and create custom data products in SAP Databricks. Data engineers can build models on a semantically rich foundation, helping produce forecasts grounded in logic that is already embedded in SAP systems while accelerating model development. 

 Build a trusted system of context across domains 

 Unified master data is only as valuable as the governance applied to it. Across the enterprise, the same customer, supplier, or product can appear differently across systems with different identifiers, attributes, and relationships. For an AI agent, understanding that these records represent the same business entity is essential for making trusted decisions. 

 Earlier this year, we announced the acquisition of Reltio , adding capabilities to help customers cleanse, harmonize, and unify data across systems. With the acquisition now complete, SAP Reltio is now generally available in SAP BDC, bringing multi-domain master data management natively into the business data fabric. 

 SAP Reltio’s AI-based entity resolution matches and reconciles records across SAP and third-party systems to create unified, 360-degree views of business entities, including customers, suppliers, products, and other critical entities. By bringing together trusted attributed, relationships and business interactions SAP Reltio gives business users and agents a more complete understanding of these entities across sources. These trusted profiles can be made available as governed data products in SAP BDC, giving Joule and Joule agents consistent, connected business context to support decisions and actions. 

 Turn enterprise knowledge into reusable business context for AI 

 Every organization operates according to a defined set of business rules, relationships, processes, and policies that determine how decisions are made. SAP Knowledge Graph provides rich business context across your data, connecting thousands of entities, relationships, and rules, creating a comprehensive view of the enterprise. Agents working on specific tasks need access to the context most relevant to the business problem they are solving, rather than the full enterprise model. 

 At SAP TechEd Berlin, we introduced SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager, a new AI-assisted experience that enables teams to create domain-specific views of SAP Knowledge Graph for applications, agents, or defined business scenarios. These curated views bring together the entities and relationships most relevant to each use case, grounding agents in the right business context they need to solve a particular business problem. 

 For example, a collections agent needs to understand customers, invoices, payment terms, and credit risk. SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager lets teams create and publish a domain view for collections. This context helps Joule Agents connect information across these business entities, supporting answers and recommendations that reflect the relationships and rules relevant to the scenario. Because these views inherit definitions and governance from SAP Knowledge Graph, teams can reuse the same business semantics in views for related use cases, such as cash flow or order management, without having to redefine those concepts. 

 Get started

 Discover how business context connects AI, actions, and outcomes 

 Getting started with SAP Business Data Cloud 

 Irfan Khan is president and chief product officer of SAP Data & Analytics.
